_comment: Firestore, Storage rules, Hosting and one Cloud Function.
The earlier note here said Hosting could not work because everything under
/api is a Node serverless function. That is still true of Hosting alone; it
is no longer true of the project, because functions/index.js now serves
those routes and the rewrites below send /api/** to it. The admin panel and
every route behind it work on Firebase exactly as they do on Vercel.
WHAT HOSTING SERVES (13 Oct 2026): the admin panel and the API behind it.
Not the website. The website is on GitHub and served by Vercel, and the
two should not be confused, because `--only hosting` deploys the whole of
public/ whatever is in it. Until today build-firebase.js filled public/
with all 31 pages, media/ and a second copy of the library's PDFs, about
480 MB, and ship.sh deployed it on every release. Hosting keeps every
version for ever and does not dedupe between them, so twenty ships in five
days reached 9.73 GB of the 10 GB that is free, while the month's total
downloads were 8.21 MB, because nobody fetches the site from here.
Two things now make that impossible to repeat, and neither depends on
anyone remembering: build-firebase.js refuses to build a bundle that could
fill the allowance, and ship.sh sets the retained version count on the
project itself on every release. Both read scripts/hosting-limits.js.
The redirects and page rewrites below are kept for `--full`, which still
builds the whole site for comparing the two deployments. In the panel
bundle their targets are not published and they simply never match.
Deploy is two steps, in this order:
node scripts/build-firebase.js
firebase deploy --only functions,hosting,firestore --project pfa-new-website
storage.rules (8 Oct 2026) refuses every browser read and write on the
Storage bucket; only the server, with admin credentials, uses it. It is
deployed on its own, because Firebase refuses it until Storage has been
switched on in the console (Build > Storage > Get started):
firebase deploy --only storage --project pfa-new-website
A bare `firebase deploy` includes it, and so fails until then.
public/ is assembled by that script from an allowlist, so no server file
can be published by accident. Never point hosting.public at '.'.
vercel.json is left untouched, so the Vercel deployment keeps working and
you can move back or run both while you compare.
